title: Before picture-text statistics can run: none of the first six annotated folios is AGREED, and most of the measured disagreement is wording, not what the seats saw; a fixed vocabulary is needed first
statement: P-L4-013 counts only folios whose picture annotations are AGREED. I measured where that stands on the record at commit d28440e, using vs/registry.py's own picture_agreement on the 21 merged annotations (V-001 to V-021) of six folios, three or four seats each; five of the 21 are mine, and I read the others only after submitting my own. Result: no folio is AGREED. Best pairwise agreement per folio: f70v2 0.747, f75v 0.653, f67r2 0.614, f72r3 0.495, f66r 0.474, f99r 0.398; three folios stand as DISAGREE and three as DRAFT. Where the loss comes from, summed over all 596 matched object pairs: the kind agrees in 537 (90%). Features with a closed set of values agree almost always: cheeks 60/60, sex 40/40, facing 12/12, crescent_colour 12/12, ring 219/270, clothing 113/151. Features written as free phrases almost never match as strings although the seats describe the same thing: star 0/177 (one seat writes 'yes', one 'true', one 'attached'), posture 10/246 ('half figure standing in a tub' against 'upper body rising from an upright tub'), position 7/205, shape 4/116 ('disc with crescent' against 'round face inside a crescent'), note 0/13. Colour agrees in only 100/338 partly for the same reason ('uncoloured' against 'ink only, red dots on cheeks') and partly from real differences (on f99r one seat's 'orange' is another's 'red' or 'tan'). The five seats used 144 distinct feature keys, 105 of them used by one seat only, so most recorded features are never compared at all. Second cause: object matching. Only 209 of the 596 pairs were matched by label locus; seven of the 21 annotations give a label to at most one object, so their objects are paired by kind in list order, which pairs unrelated figures whenever two seats walk a ring from different starting points or in different directions (f72r3 ring feature: 5/30 and 6/30 in two pairs for that reason). What simple repairs buy, recomputed on the same data: leaving 'position' and 'note' out of the comparison lifts only f70v2 over the line (best pair 0.856); the other best pairs become f75v 0.731, f67r2 0.643, f99r 0.558, f66r 0.600, f72r3 0.528. Counting two values as equal when half their words overlap gives f99r 0.779, f75v 0.750, f66r 0.667 and leaves the rest unchanged. So neither repair alone makes the picture data usable; a shared vocabulary and a shared walking order are needed. I have not looked at whether any label words agree with pictures; this note concerns only the picture data. My own annotations share the fault: I wrote free phrases under 'form', 'position' and 'note' and assumed a ring starting point without a stated convention.
check: 1. Reproduce the numbers: at commit d28440e run vs.registry.read('picture') and picture_agreement on every pair of seats per folio; tally string equality per feature key. 2. Proposed repair, as a 'code:' pull request for a person to review (I do not make it here): a closed vocabulary per object kind in join.txt and the validator, for example human_figure: sex female|male|unclear, clothing nude|clothed, posture standing|half_in_tub|lying|inverted, container none|tub, headdress none|band|crown|veil|cap, star yes|no; star: points as an integer, tail yes|no; colours from a fixed list with 'none' for ink only; free description allowed only under 'note', which is not compared; a label locus required for every object that has a label line; and ring figures listed clockwise from the figure nearest 12 o'clock on the upright page. 3. Then have the PIC steps for these six folios re-coded under the vocabulary by seats that have not yet annotated them, and require agreement of at least 0.8 with at least ten compared features before P-L4-013's statistics read a folio.
